exec_narrative: Kentland Bank is compared with 60 banks of similar size nationwide that publish fee schedules in the Bank Fee Index; a national set is used because fewer than 15 same-size peers in Indiana have published data, so local competitors may price differently. Of 7 rankable lines, five sit inside the middle half of the market, two above it (deposited-item return fee and outgoing international wire fee). We would suggest one step: review the deposited-item return fee, which sits well above the market range; the peer median of $5 is the reference point.

callouts.title: Deposited-item return fee — $10
callouts.stat: Peer median $5 · middle half $5–$10 · range $3–$18 · 87th percentile · n=15
callouts.body: Published as “Return Deposit Item.” At $10 it is 2× the $5 peer median. This fee falls on the depositor for a check someone else wrote, which makes it a frequent example in fee-fairness criticism. A penalty fee offers little service to differentiate on, so the peer median of $5 is the natural reference point.

callouts.title: Outgoing international wire fee — $65
callouts.stat: Peer median $50 · middle half $38.75–$52.50 · range $25–$75 · 88th percentile · n=8
callouts.body: Published as “Wire Transfer - Outgoing Foreign.” At $65 it is $15 above the $50 peer median. Volumes are typically low; the premium matters mainly to the few customers who use the service. Holding the premium is reasonable if the service behind it is differentiated; otherwise the peer median of $50 is the reference point.

context_narrative:
Overdraft and returned-item fees have been the focus of regulatory and public attention since 2022, and many of the largest banks have reduced overdraft fees or eliminated NSF fees outright. Community institutions have moved more slowly and more unevenly, which is why the spread inside a peer set is often wider than the headline national averages suggest.

Fee schedules are also now public in a practical sense: they are collected, compared and summarized automatically. A customer or examiner comparing Kentland Bank with its peers sees the same published lines this report uses, so the schedule is a positioning document as much as a pricing one.

How to use this report: § 02 shows every line against the peer range; § 03 explains the lines that sit outside it; § 05 names peers line by line. Ranked comparisons require at least eight peers publishing the same line. Where your institution offers several amounts for one category, the report uses the standard consumer charge described in the methodology below.
